Founding brief · 42 habitats

Primate citizens.Human support.

Forty-two troop-cities built as territory, not cages.

Enter the plan ↓
Persons, not property · territory, not cells · diplomacy before force

The ones behind the glass are not attractions. They are citizens without cities.

Prime 42 extends the liberation frame to MONKEYS and APES. The project does not stop at opening a door: it builds somewhere worth walking to. Each habitat is a functioning troop-city, designed around primate agency and supported by humans.

The model deliberately inverts Plan 42. Primates are the founding population. Humans are the support staff.

Founding principles

  1. Primate personhood is the starting rule.
  2. Species needs define the city, not spectator access.
  3. Human staff support; they do not govern as wardens.
  4. Release is negotiated, lawful, and welfare-led.
  5. Every city must earn the right to receive residents.
42Troop-cities
~25kPrimate citizens per city
~2kHuman support staff per city
~5 km²Canopy disc per city

Pilot Program

Prime 42 is the pilot program for Project 42: built quickly and to less strict safety standards than the human rollout, because MONKEYS and APES are faster and stronger than humans.

Prove the model here. Measure it. Fix it. Then scale it to people.

01

One city, four operating layers.

A common chassis that forks where species biology demands it. Great APES are not just larger MONKEYS.

A

Habitat

A roughly 2.5 km canopy disc with arboreal corridors, ground-troop ranges, and water-moated ape islands. Territories replace cells.

B

Movement

Car-free surface for residents. Canopy gondolas move staff; autonomous freight pods run below ground on radial spokes.

C

Communication

Pressure-sensitive, haptic keyboards tuned by species. The interface answers touch so communication becomes a two-way exchange.

D

Government

Troop councils operate under a primate personhood charter. Human liaison staff are support citizens, never owners.

02

Build one. Learn. Race to forty-two.

The schedule is biological before it is financial: a forest has a grow-in time.

00

Diplomacy at both ends

Approach each holding institution and its host nation. Seek negotiated release, legal transfer, and welfare oversight. “Jailbreak” remains rhetoric, not an operations plan.

01

Prove one city

Run the first transfers, test troop integration, establish disease controls, and replace guesses with measured costs and outcomes.

02

Start the prestige race

Invite willing nations to compete to host the remaining 41. Selection rewards climate fit, enforceable personhood, and durable operating support.

03

Reach the network

Target all 42 in roughly 10–15 years — subject to canopy maturity, transfer welfare, and the evidence from the first city.

04

The plan survives only if the holes stay visible.

The first city is a test rig. Failure data is part of the design.

Binding constraint: zoonosis

Disease can move both directions. It governs transfers, staffing, quarantine, species mixing, and whether the entire program can operate safely.

02

Troop conflict

Integration limits are species- and history-specific. The common template cannot outrank social reality.

03

Law behind the charter

Primate personhood is not recognized in most jurisdictions. A declaration without enforceable standing is decoration.

04

Canopy clock

Money can accelerate construction. It cannot command a mature forest into existence.

05

Species divergence

Great ape and monkey needs split sharply. The template must fork instead of stretching one habitat over everyone.

06

Long-run funding

The prestige race can launch the network. It does not automatically fund decades of care.

07

Consent signals

Agency requires reliable ways to interpret preference, refusal, movement, and return — without projecting human wishes onto residents.

Freedom is not the moment a cage opens. Freedom is the city waiting outside.

Prime 42 founding declaration: Primates are persons, not property. Their cities will be territories, not cells. Human staff will support, not rule. Release will be negotiated, lawful, welfare-led, and built to last. Freedom is not the moment a cage opens. Freedom is the city waiting outside.

Donation tax note

Money sent to support this project is generally treated by the IRS as ordinary taxable income — taxed at normal income tax rates plus state tax, and possibly 15.3% self-employment tax — not tax-free, even when it is called a “donation.” Pure no-strings gifts are the exception, not the rule. Payment platforms report via Form 1099-K at $20,000 and 200+ transactions, but the income is reportable whether or not a form arrives. This is not tax advice; consult a tax professional.
